extracted.intended_audience: Postsecondary institutions and other recipients of Federal financial assistance; Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and higher-education compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards that postsecondary institutions must follow when handling complaints of sex discrimination and sex-based harassment involving student complainants or respondents, including notice, investigation, hearing, determination, remedies, appeals, and related employment and anti-retaliation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for determination whether sex discrimination occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the preponderance of the evidence standard of proof to determine whether sex discrimination occurred, unless the recipient uses the clear and convincing evidence standard of proof in all other comparable proceedings, in which case the recipient may elect that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both standards require the decisionmaker to evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness; if the decisionmaker is not persuaded under the applicable standard, whatever the quantity of the evidence is, the decisionmaker must not determine that sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the parties in writing of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred including the rationale for such determination, and the procedures and permissible bases for the complainant and respondent to appeal, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be simultaneous to parties where required elsewhere in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies, sanctions coordination, and discipline prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a determination that sex discrimination occurred, require the Title IX Coordinator to coordinate provision and implementation of remedies to complainants and other persons identified as harmed, coordinate imposition of disciplinary sanctions on a respondent, and take other prompt and effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may not impose discipline on a respondent for Title IX-prohibited sex discrimination unless there is a determination at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures that the respondent engaged in prohibited sex discrimination; must comply with §§106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46 before imposing any disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections against disciplining participants for false statements or consensual sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not discipline a party, witness, or others participating in grievance procedures for making a false statement or for engaging in consensual sexual conduct based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals parity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer the parties an appeal process that, at a minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, including proceedings relating to other discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent, a postsecondary institution must also offer an appeal on the bases set out in §106.46(i)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional grievance provisions must apply equally
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts additional provisions as part of its grievance procedures for handling complaints of sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment, such additional provisions must apply equally to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional informal resolution consistent with §106.44(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of resolving a complaint through grievance procedures, parties may elect to participate in an informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if provided by the recipient consistent with that paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered or provided, the postsecondary institution must inform the parties in writing of the offer and their rights and responsibilities and otherwise comply with §106.44(k)(3) in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures and sanctions/remedies disclosure for sex-based harassment complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: For complaints alleging sex-based harassment, the grievance procedures must describe the range of supportive measures available and list or describe the range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies the recipient may impose or provide following a determination that sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.44(g) for supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of §106.45 and §106.46 in postsecondary grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures for prompt and equitable resolution of sex-based harassment involving students must include provisions that incorporate the requirements of §106.45 and this section (§106.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-employee applicability inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant or respondent is both a student and an employee, the institution must make a fact-specific inquiry to determine whether the requirements of this section apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, consider whether the party's primary relationship with the institution is to receive an education and whether the alleged harassment occurred while performing employment-related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations content
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon initiation of sex-based harassment grievance procedures, provide written notice to known parties with sufficient time to prepare before any initial interview; the written notice must include all information required under §106.45(c)(1)(i)-(iii) and additionally inform parties that the respondent is presumed not responsible, advisors may be chosen and may be attorneys, parties are entitled to equal opportunity to access relevant evidence or an investigative report, and, if applicable, the code of conduct prohibits knowingly making false statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the institution provides an investigative report, parties are entitled to equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of additional allegations and permissible delay for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional allegations are investigated that were not included in the initial written notice, the recipient must provide written notice of the additional allegations to known parties; the recipient may reasonably delay providing written notice if it has reasonable concerns for the safety of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable concerns must be based on individualized safety and risk analysis and not on mere speculation or stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal notice and complainant withdrawal documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When dismissing a complaint alleging sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent, provide the parties simultaneously with written notice of the dismissal and the basis for the dismissal, except if dismissal occurs before the respondent has been notified, then provide such written notice only to the complainant; obtain the complainant's withdrawal in writing if dismissing based on the complainant's voluntary withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of meetings and proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must provide, to a party whose participation is invited or expected, written notice of the date, time, location, participants, and purpose of all meetings or proceedings with sufficient time for the party to prepare to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor parity and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the parties with the same opportunities to be accompanied to any meeting or proceeding by the advisor of their choice, who may be, but is not required to be, an attorney, and do not limit the choice or presence of the advisor for either party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution may establish restrictions regarding the extent the advisor may participate, as long as restrictions apply equally to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to have other persons present
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the parties with the same opportunities, if any, to have persons other than the advisor of the parties' choice present during any meeting or proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witness determination applied equally
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution has discretion to determine whether the parties may present expert witnesses so long as the determination applies equally to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable extensions of timeframes for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow reasonable extension of timeframes on a case-by-case basis for good cause with written notice to the parties that includes the reason for the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to evidence and investigative reports; opportunity to review and respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide each party and the party's advisor with an equal opportunity to access evidence relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible, either by access to the evidence or to the same written investigative report that accurately summarizes the evidence, and provide a reasonable opportunity to review and respond to that evidence or report prior to the determination whether sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a live hearing is conducted, the opportunity to review evidence must be provided in advance of the live hearing; the institution may decide whether response opportunity occurs prior to the hearing, during the hearing, or both. Take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosure of information obtained solely through the sex-based harassment grievance procedures. Compliance satisfies §106.45(f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for questioning parties and witnesses to assess credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a process that enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility where credibility is in dispute and relevant, consistent with the specified provisions for non-live and live hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questioning must take place before determining whether sex-based harassment occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-live hearing question procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When not conducting a live hearing, allow the investigator or decisionmaker to ask relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions and follow-up questions during individual meetings; allow each party to propose questions to be asked by the investigator/decisionmaker; provide each party with an audio/audiovisual recording or transcript with enough time to propose follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include those challenging credibility; proposals and follow-ups are subject to the requirements in paragraph (f)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing question procedures and advisor-conducted questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting a live hearing, allow the decisionmaker to ask questions and either (A) allow each party to propose questions for the decisionmaker to ask, or (B) allow each party's advisor to ask any party or witness such questions, subject to relevance determinations. Questioning must never be conducted by a party personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advisor-conducted questioning is permitted and a party lacks an advisor, the institution must provide an advisor of the institution's choice, without charge, for the purpose of questioning; in those instances the institution must not appoint a confidential employee and may appoint, but is not required to appoint, an attorney to serve as advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker review and limitation of proposed questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker must determine whether a proposed question is relevant under §106.2 and not otherwise impermissible under §106.45(b)(7) prior to the question being posed, and must explain any decision to exclude a question as not relevant or otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question is unclear or harassing, the decisionmaker must give the party an opportunity to clarify or revise the question; if sufficiently clarified, the question must be asked. Institutions may adopt other reasonable decorum rules provided they apply equally to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to respond to questions and permissible inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker may choose to place less or no weight on statements by a party or witness who refuses to respond to relevant and not impermissible questions, but must not draw an inference about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a refusal to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing format and recording requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's sex-based harassment grievance procedures may provide for a live hearing conducted with parties physically present in the same location or physically present in separate locations with technology enabling simultaneous seeing and hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution must create an audio or audiovisual recording or transcript of any live hearing and make it available to the parties for inspection and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination content and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the determination whether sex-based harassment occurred in writing to the parties simultaneously, and include: (i) a description of the alleged harassment; (ii) information about the policies and procedures used to evaluate the allegations; (iii) the decisionmaker's evaluation of the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence and determination; (iv) when harassment is found, any disciplinary sanctions and remedies to be provided and, to the extent appropriate, other students identified as experiencing effects; and (v) the institution's procedures for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination regarding responsibility becomes final either on the date the institution provides parties with the written determination of the result of any appeal, or, if no party appeals, the date on which an appeal would no longer be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals bases for postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must offer the parties an appeal from a determination or dismissal on the following bases: (i) procedural irregularity that would change the outcome; (ii) new evidence that would change the outcome and was not reasonably available earlier; (iii) the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker had a conflict of interest or bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution may offer additional bases so long as procedures and additional bases are equally available to all parties; must comply with §106.45(d)(3)(i),(v),(vi) in writing for all appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution written notice and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a postsecondary institution offers or provides an informal resolution process under §106.44(k), it must inform the parties in writing of the offer and their rights and responsibilities in that process and otherwise comply with §106.44(k)(3) in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary review limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary will not deem a recipient to have violated this part solely because the Assistant Secretary would have reached a different determination in a particular complaint than the recipient reached under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46, based on the Assistant Secretary's independent weighing of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment nondiscrimination regarding leaves and related matters
rubrics_metrics.description: In employment, recipients must not discriminate on the basis of sex with respect to granting and return from leaves of absence, leave for pregnancy or related conditions, leave for persons of either sex to care for children or dependents, or any other leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.51(b)(6) revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental, family, or marital status nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not adopt or implement any policy, practice, or procedure, or take any employment action, on the basis of sex concerning current, potential, or past parental, family, or marital status that treats persons differently, or that is based upon whether an employee is head of household or principal wage earner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy and related conditions protections
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions, and must treat pregnancy or related conditions as any other temporary medical conditions for all job-related purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes commencement, duration and extensions of leave; payment of disability income; accrual of seniority; reinstatement; and fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary leave of absence for pregnancy-related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not maintain a leave policy or an employee lacks sufficient leave, treat pregnancy or related conditions as justification for a voluntary unpaid leave for a reasonable period, at the conclusion of which the employee shall be reinstated to the prior status or a comparable position without decrease in compensation, loss of promotional opportunities, or other rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation break time and space
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide reasonable break time for an employee to express breast milk or breastfeed as needed and ensure access to a lactation space that is a space other than a bathroom that is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-employment inquiry restrictions: marital status and sex
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not make a pre-employment inquiry as to the marital status of an applicant; a recipient may ask an applicant to self-identify their sex only if asked of all applicants and the response is not used as a basis for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marital-status inquiries include asking whether an applicant is 'Miss or Mrs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibition and grievance initiation obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must prohibit retaliation, including peer retaliation, in its education program or activity; when the recipient has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute retaliation under Title IX, the recipient is obligated to comply with §106.44 and must initiate its grievance procedures under §106.45 or an informal resolution under §106.44(k) upon receiving a complaint alleging retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the complaint is consolidated with a sex-based harassment complaint involving students at a postsecondary institution, the consolidated grievance procedures must comply with the requirements of both §§106.45 and 106.46.
